title: Introduction to Biology — University Program
summary: A one-term foundation in cell and molecular biology.

outcomes: The learner can explain the cell theory and the scientific method.
The learner can trace energy flow through respiration and photosynthesis.
The learner can predict simple Mendelian inheritance outcomes.
The learner can describe how DNA is copied and expressed.
The learner can explain evolution by natural selection.

handoff.input: Design an introductory university Biology 101 course for first-year students with no college chemistry. Cover the scientific method, the chemistry of life, cell structure, membranes and transport, energy and enzymes, cellular respiration, photosynthesis, mitosis, meiosis, Mendelian genetics, DNA structure and replication, gene expression, and evolution by natural selection. Depth: introductory but rigorous; connect every topic to a worked example and a real-world observation. Exclude organic-chemistry reaction mechanisms and detailed biochemistry pathways beyond glycolysis/Krebs/electron transport at an overview level. 13 weeks, two 50-minute lectures per week.

audience.notes: First-year university; no prior college chemistry assumed.
